cards.text: The LORD is still speaking to Moses, Israel's leader, and now He's handing out the calendar. He tells Moses to say to the Israelites, “These are My appointed feasts, the feasts of the LORD that you are to proclaim as sacred assemblies.” Friend, this might be the first schedule in history that people actually look FORWARD to.
First on God's list is the one that comes every week. For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a day of sacred assembly.

cards.question: True or false: Israelites who live far from the sacred assembly don't have to keep the Sabbath.

cards.text: Then come the LORD's appointed feasts at their appointed times, starting with the Passover to the LORD at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. God gives an EXACT start time, friend, and I can't even get my own oven timer to go off when I want it to.

cards.question: On the fifteenth day of that same month, a seven-day feast begins. What kind of bread does God say Israel must eat all seven days?
The Feast of Unleavened Bread opens with a sacred assembly and no regular work. True or false: Its seventh day is a sacred assembly with no regular work too.

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses another message, this one for a day that's still coming. When Israel enters the land He's giving them and reaps its harvest, they bring the priest a sheaf of the firstfruits, and he waves it before the LORD on the day after the Sabbath.

cards.question: The priest waves the first sheaf of the harvest before the LORD so that it may be ___ on Israel's behalf.

cards.text: That same day, a year-old lamb without blemish goes up as a burnt offering, with fine flour mixed with oil and a drink offering of wine. God calls it a pleasing aroma.

cards.question: True or false: Once the harvest comes in, Israel can start eating the new grain before that first sheaf has been brought to God.

cards.text: From the day the sheaf is waved, Israel counts off seven full weeks. Seven weeks? Friend, I sat in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS with nothing to count but dust.

cards.question: Seven full weeks, right up to the day after the seventh Sabbath. In all, Israel counts off ___ days and then brings the LORD an offering of new grain.

cards.text: Then Israel brings two loaves of bread from their homes, baked with leaven, as firstfruits to the LORD, along with lambs, a young bull, rams and a goat. The priest waves the bread and two of the lambs before the LORD, and they're holy to the LORD for the priest.

cards.question: On the day Israel brings the new grain, God gives one more instruction for that day. What is it?

answers.text: Hold a sacred assembly with no regular work
Bring every lamb they own to the priest
Stay awake through the whole night

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of the feasts, God gives a harvest rule: don't reap all the way to the edges of the field, and don't gather the gleanings. Friend, I've chased the LAST crumb across a cooling rack with my mustache, so I know this is a big ask.

cards.question: God tells Israel to leave the edges of the field and the gleanings of the harvest. Who are they left for?

answers.text: The poor and the foreign resident

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again, and the calendar jumps to the seventh month. On the first day of that month, Israel gets a day of rest and a sacred assembly, announced by something LOUD.

cards.question: What announces the day of rest and sacred assembly on the first day of the seventh month?

cards.text: Trumpet blasts, friend! Ruby, one of my cookie cutter kids, is shaped like a bell, and when she had something to say, the WHOLE kitchen we shared stopped to listen. That day, Israel does no regular work and presents a food offering to the LORD.
Then the LORD speaks to Moses again: the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement.

cards.question: On the Day of Atonement, Israel holds a sacred assembly, presents a food offering to the LORD, and is told to ___ themselves.
True or false: On the Day of Atonement, a little regular work is fine once the sacred assembly is over.

cards.text: No work, because it's the Day of Atonement, when atonement is made for them before the LORD their God. And the stakes are high: anyone who doesn't humble himself must be cut off from his people, and anyone who does any work on this day, God says He will destroy from among his people.

cards.question: God calls the Day of Atonement a Sabbath of complete rest. When does that Sabbath begin?

answers.text: The evening of the ninth day

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses once more: on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the Feast of Tabernacles to the LORD begins, and it runs seven days. Seven DAYS, friend? I get winded stamping seven cookies.

cards.question: True or false: When the seven days of the Feast of Tabernacles are done, there's still an eighth day, and it's a solemn assembly.

cards.text: Then God wraps up the list: these are His appointed feasts, each with its own offerings on its own designated day. And all of that comes on top of the Sabbath offerings, the gifts, the vow offerings and the freewill offerings.
But God circles back to the Feast of Tabernacles for a little more. It comes after Israel has gathered the produce of the land, with complete rest on the first day and on the eighth.

cards.question: On the first day of the Feast of Tabernacles, God tells Israel to gather something. What is it?
The harvest is in and the branches are gathered. Then God tells Israel to ___ before the LORD their God for seven days.

cards.text: Then comes the camping part. For seven days, all the native-born of Israel must dwell in booths, and friend, after years in a junk drawer, a booth sounds like a BEACH HOUSE to me.

cards.question: God brought Israel out of Egypt. Why does He want them living in booths for seven days every year?

answers.text: So later generations know God had Israel live in booths
So they can stay close to their fields at harvest
So their houses are free for travelers that week

cards.question: True or false: Moses keeps the appointed feasts of the LORD to himself and tells only the priests.

cards.text: So Moses announces the appointed feasts of the LORD to the Israelites, and the calendar is FULL. But God's not done teaching His people how to be holy, friend, so stick with me.
